prompt: Solid-state battery commercialization timeline and the remaining technical challenges
report:
# Solid-State Batteries: Timeline and Challenges

## Why solid-state
Replacing the liquid electrolyte with a solid electrolyte promises higher energy density, faster charging, and reduced fire risk versus today's lithium-ion cells [S1][S2].

## Commercialization timeline
Toyota targets limited production of solid-state cells for EVs around 2027-2028 [S3], while QuantumScape and Samsung SDI report multilayer cell samples shipping to automakers for qualification [S4][S5]. Most analysts expect meaningful volume only late this decade [S6].

## Remaining challenges
The hardest problem is dendrite penetration through the solid electrolyte during fast charging, which shorts the cell [S7][S8]. Manufacturing defect-free thin electrolyte layers at scale and maintaining interface contact under cycling stress remain unsolved at low cost [S8][S9]. Achieving the promised energy density while keeping cycle life high is still a trade-off [S2][S9].

## Outlook
Solid-state is a when-not-if technology; dendrite suppression and scalable electrolyte manufacturing gate the timeline [S6][S8].
